summary: An Islamic monarchy on the northern coast of Borneo, where the Sultan holds real power, and which has become a high-income country on the strength of oil and natural gas.

ranking.name: Islam (Sunni)
ranking.description: Islam is generally thought to have been introduced to northern Borneo in the 14th–15th centuries by Arab, Indian and Chinese Muslim merchants through maritime trade, and tradition holds that in the late 14th century the ruler of Brunei converted to Islam and became the first sultan, Muhammad Shah, so that Brunei became a sultanate. The Brunei Sultanate reached the height of its power in the 16th century, and Islam took root among the Malays; the 1959 constitution made Islam (the Sunni Shafi'i school) the state religion, and since 2014 Islamic criminal law has been implemented in stages.

ranking.name: Christianity
ranking.description: Christians are mainly Chinese, some indigenous people and foreign workers. After British influence in Borneo grew in the 19th century, Anglican and Catholic missionaries began preaching in the area around Brunei. Because Brunei strictly restricts proselytizing by other religions, the number of Christians has always been small, and they cannot celebrate Christmas openly.

ranking.name: Buddhism
ranking.description: Buddhists are mainly in the Chinese community, whose ancestors moved to Brunei from Fujian, Guangdong and elsewhere in China in the 19th–20th centuries to work in commerce and labor. The Chinese usually blend Buddhism, Taoism and folk beliefs, and the Teng Yun Temple in Bandar Seri Begawan is the center of Chinese religious life.

ranking.name: Other (indigenous beliefs, etc.)
ranking.description: Other religions include the indigenous animist beliefs, preserved mainly in the interior by Borneo indigenous peoples such as the Iban and the Dusun, who worship nature spirits and ancestral spirits. With the policy of Islamization and with modernization, many indigenous people have converted to Islam or Christianity, and the proportion of traditional beliefs continues to fall.

religion.background: Before the arrival of Islam, Brunei was influenced by Hindu and Buddhist culture, and 'Boni', recorded in Chinese histories, may be the predecessor of Brunei. In the 14th–15th centuries the rulers of Brunei converted to Islam and the Brunei Sultanate soon rose, and in the 16th century its power extended across northern Borneo and the southern Philippines. In 1888 Brunei became a British protectorate, and after oil was discovered in 1929 its economy developed rapidly. After independence in 1984, Brunei took the 'Malay Islamic Monarchy' (Melayu Islam Beraja) as its national philosophy, and since 2014 it has gradually implemented Islamic criminal law, making it one of the most religiously oriented countries in Southeast Asia.

ranking.name: Malay (Brunei Malay)
ranking.description: Malay is the official language of Brunei, and Brunei Malay is the local dialect, which differs from Standard Malay in pronunciation and vocabulary. The Brunei Sultanate has used Malay as the language of the court and administration since the 14th–15th centuries, and the 1959 constitution made it the official language; the government promotes the 'Malay Islamic Monarchy' as the national philosophy, of which Malay is a core part. About 70% of the population use Malay as their main language.

ranking.name: Chinese (Hokkien, Hakka, Mandarin, etc.)
ranking.description: Chinese speakers are mainly ethnic Chinese, whose ancestors moved to Brunei from Fujian and Guangdong in the late 19th and early 20th centuries; the most common dialects are Hokkien and Hakka, while Mandarin spread through Chinese-language school education. Chinese schools in Brunei, such as Chung Hwa Middle School, were founded in the first half of the 20th century and remain important institutions for the Chinese community to preserve its language and culture.

ranking.name: English
ranking.description: English became the language of administration and commerce during the British protectorate of 1888–1984, and from 1985 Brunei implemented a bilingual education policy, with mathematics and science taught in English from secondary school upward. English is therefore widely used in education, commerce and law, but only about 5% have English as their mother tongue.

language.history: The indigenous peoples of the Brunei area use many Austronesian languages, such as Dusun and Iban. After the Brunei Sultanate was established in the 14th–15th centuries, Malay became the language of the court, trade and Islam, and was written in Jawi (Malay in Arabic script). After becoming a British protectorate in 1888, English entered administration and education, and Malay in the Roman alphabet also gradually spread. After independence in 1984, Brunei adopted 'bilingual education' and preserved Jawi as a symbol of national culture; street signs and shop signs must also display Jawi.

ranking.name: Ambuyat
ranking.description: Sago palm starch is stirred with hot water into a transparent, sticky paste, rolled up with a special bamboo fork and dipped in a sour and spicy sauce, with a slippery texture.
ranking.history: Ambuyat is regarded as the national dish of Brunei. The sago palm is a plant native to the swamps of Borneo, and for thousands of years the indigenous peoples have eaten its starch as a staple. In the past, when rice was short, ambuyat was an important source of food, and it is said that during the Japanese occupation of Brunei in the Second World War (1941–1945), many people relied on ambuyat to get through the food shortage. Today it is a traditional dish that Bruneians share with family and friends, and the way of rolling it up with the bamboo fork 'candas' is distinctive.

ranking.name: Nasi katok
ranking.description: A simple portion of white rice with a piece of fried chicken or chicken curry, plus a little sambal chili paste, wrapped in paper to take away, and cheap.
ranking.history: Nasi katok has been Brunei's most popular cheap takeaway meal since the 1980s; the 'katok' in the name means 'knock' in Malay, and it is said to come from the early days when people knocked on shop doors late at night to buy this simple meal. Because the portion is just right and it is cheap, it has become an everyday meal for Bruneian students, office workers and families. Bruneians often regard it as the most representative 'taste of Brunei'.

ranking.name: Nasi lemak
ranking.description: Fragrant rice cooked with coconut milk and pandan leaf, served with sambal, fried anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and boiled egg, savory and mildly spicy.
ranking.history: Nasi lemak is a traditional dish shared across the Malay world, with origins linked to the fishing villages of the Malay Peninsula, where fishermen ate nasi lemak for breakfast to give them strength for working at sea. Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia all regard it as a local tradition. In Brunei it is a common breakfast, often sold wrapped in banana leaf in a triangle shape.

ranking.name: Satay
ranking.description: Chicken or beef marinated in spices is skewered on bamboo sticks and grilled over charcoal, served with a rich peanut sauce, cucumber, onion and rice cakes, with an intoxicating aroma.
ranking.history: Satay is generally thought to originate in Java, Indonesia, where in the 19th century it was probably influenced by the kebab brought by Arab and Indian merchants, developing a version seasoned with peanut sauce. Through trade and migration in the Malay world, satay spread to Brunei, Malaysia and Singapore. In Brunei it is one of the most popular snacks at night markets and festivals.

ranking.name: Beef rendang
ranking.description: Beef is slowly stewed for a long time with coconut milk, lemongrass, galangal, chili and other spices until the liquid reduces and the meat is well flavored, dark brown in color.
ranking.history: Rendang originates from the Minangkabau people of Sumatra, Indonesia, whose tradition is long-distance migration (merantau), and rendang became a travel food because it keeps for weeks. With the migration and trade of the Minangkabau, rendang spread across the Malay world. In Brunei it is an essential festive dish in every household at Hari Raya Aidilfitri, served to relatives and friends together with lemang and ketupat.
